title: Step 1 · Before Umrah
text: step 1 of 8 before umrah 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 step 01 before umrah get your papers, your body and your heart ready. where am i? at home, before you travel what do i do now? open the “before you go” planner a countdown from 8 weeks to the day you travel, nusuk step by step, and health tips for the heat. tick as you go. your ticks are saved on this phone. papers visa. umrah is allowed on an umrah visa or a saudi visit/tourist visa. umrah permit in the nusuk app. book your umrah time slot in the official nusuk app. you can’t enter for umrah before your permit time. passport valid for at least 6 months from your travel date. confirm with your airline or agent. meningitis vaccine (all pilgrims). acyw or acywx conjugate vaccine within the last 5 years (or polysaccharide within 3 years), at least 10 days before arrival. only if it applies to you: polio or yellow fever vaccines for arrivals from listed countries (pakistan and afghanistan are on the polio list). covid-19 proof for people over 65, pregnant women and those with chronic illness. hotel address and group leader’s number, saved on your phone and on paper. checked september 2026 · health: saudi ministry of health, umrah health requirements 1447h (2026) · permits and visas: ministry of hajj and umrah faq · passport: travel industry guidance. rules can change each season; check again before booking. bookings (nusuk and travel) create your nusuk account (official app of the ministry of hajj and umrah). all permits and umrah bookings run through it. umrah visa: hotel booked through nusuk masar. since the 1447h season, a confirmed booking in a licensed hotel, recorded in nusuk masar, is required before an umrah visa is issued. your agent or nusuk does this. umrah permit for your chosen date and time, in the nusuk app (see papers above). train (optional): the haramain high speed railway links jeddah airport (king abdulaziz international), jeddah, makkah and madinah. makkah to madinah takes about 2 hours. book only through the official saudi arabia railways (sar) channels. visiting madinah? book a rawdah (riyad al-jannah) permit in the nusuk app. it is free; men and women have separate times and gates; you can only enter in your booked slot. checked september 2026 · nusuk masar hotel rule: ministry of hajj and umrah (reported by saudi gazette, june 2025) · train: saudi arabia railways / visit saudi · rawdah: nusuk app rules as reported september 2026. booking rules change often; check in the nusuk app before you travel. pack men: 2 plain white ihram sheets, a belt, open sandals. women: loose, modest clothes that cover the body. any colour. unscented soap, shampoo and deodorant (for use in ihram). your medicines in original packs, with prescriptions. small bag, water bottle, power bank, a bag for your shoes. heart & mind learn the 4 essential acts: ihram, tawaf, sa‘i, hair. practise the talbiyah (see step 2). renew your intention, repent, settle debts, ask forgiveness from people you may have wronged. what do i say? leaving your home بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللَّهِ، لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ bismillāh, tawakkaltu ‘ala-llāh, lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh. meaning: in the name of allah. i put my trust in allah. there is no might nor power except with allah. sunan abi dawud 5095 (sahih) setting off on the journey (full travel dua) اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ. سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ، وَإِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ. اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّا نَسْأَلُكَ فِي سَفَرِنَا هَذَا الْبِرَّ وَالتَّقْوَى، وَمِنَ الْعَمَلِ مَا تَرْضَى. اللَّهُمَّ هَوِّنْ عَلَيْنَا سَفَرَنَا هَذَا وَاطْوِ عَنَّا بُعْدَهُ. اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ الصَّاحِبُ فِي السَّفَرِ، وَالْخَلِيفَةُ فِي الْأَهْلِ. اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ وَعْثَاءِ السَّفَرِ، وَكَآبَةِ الْمَنْظَرِ، وَسُوءِ الْمُنْقَلَبِ فِي الْمَالِ وَالْأَهْلِ allāhu akbar (×3). subḥāna-lladhī sakhkhara lanā hādhā wa mā kunnā lahū muqrinīn, wa innā ilā rabbinā la-munqalibūn. allāhumma innā nas’aluka fī safarinā hādha-l-birra wa-t-taqwā, wa mina-l-‘amali mā tarḍā. allāhumma hawwin ‘alaynā safaranā hādhā wa-ṭwi ‘annā bu‘dah. allāhumma anta-ṣ-ṣāḥibu fi-s-safar, wa-l-khalīfatu fi-l-ahl. allāhumma innī a‘ūdhu bika min wa‘thā’i-s-safar, wa ka’ābati-l-manẓar, wa sū’i-l-munqalabi fi-l-māli wa-l-ahl. meaning: allah is the greatest (three times). glory be to the one who has placed this at our service; we could not have done it ourselves, and to our lord we will surely return. o allah, we ask you on this journey for goodness and piety, and for deeds that please you. o allah, make this journey easy for us and shorten its distance. o allah, you are the companion on the journey and the one who looks after the family. o allah, i seek refuge in you from the hardship of travel, from distressing sights, and from an evil return to wealth and family. sahih muslim 1342 remember men: practise wearing ihram at home try tying the sheets and belt once before you travel. expect a lot of walking sa‘i alone is about 3 km. break in comfortable sandals before you go. avoid leaving all the learning until you arrive. you will be tired. packing only scented toiletries. you can’t use them in ihram. map next · step 2 enter ihram

title: Step 2 · Ihram
text: step 2 of 8 ihram 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 step 02 · essential ihram الإحرام the sacred state of umrah. you enter it with an intention and the talbiyah . the clothes alone are not ihram. where am i? before you pass the meeqat the meeqat is a boundary you must not cross without ihram. on a plane, the crew usually announces it. your group leader will tell you which one you pass. the five meeqat dhul-hulayfah (abyar ‘ali) coming from madinah al-juhfah (rabigh) coming from the north-west: syria, egypt, north africa qarn al-manazil (as-sayl al-kabir) coming from najd and the east yalamlam (as-sa‘diyyah) coming from yemen and the south dhat ‘irq coming from iraq already in makkah? go outside the haram boundary, e.g. masjid ‘a’ishah at tan‘im, and enter ihram there. sahih al-bukhari 1524, sahih muslim 1181; dhat ‘irq: sahih al-bukhari 1531 what do i do now? 1 get clean. trim nails, remove unwanted hair, take a full bath (ghusl). men may put perfume on the body, not the clothes, before the intention. sunnah 2 put on ihram clothes. see “men” and “women” below. must 3 pray, if it is a prayer time. it is good to enter ihram after a prayer. scholars differ many scholars recommend 2 rak‘ahs for ihram; others say there is no special ihram prayer. 4 at or before the meeqat, make the intention. intend umrah in your heart and say: “labbayka ‘umratan.” must 5 say the talbiyah often. men aloud, women quietly. keep saying it until you begin tawaf. sunnah men two white, unstitched sheets: one round the waist, one over the shoulders. head uncovered. open sandals. women your normal loose, modest clothes, any colour. no niqab and no gloves. more for women what do i say? 1 · intention at the meeqat لَبَّيْكَ عُمْرَةً labbayka ‘umratan meaning: here i am, o allah, for umrah. based on the prophet’s ﷺ wording “labbayka ‘umratan wa ḥajjan” for umrah with hajj · sahih muslim 1251 2 · talbiyah, again and again لَبَّيْكَ اللَّهُمَّ لَبَّيْكَ، لَبَّيْكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ لَبَّيْكَ، إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ وَالنِّعْمَةَ لَكَ وَالْمُلْكَ، لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ labbayka-llāhumma labbayk. labbayka lā sharīka laka labbayk. inna-l-ḥamda wa-n-ni‘mata laka wa-l-mulk. lā sharīka lak. meaning: here i am, o allah, here i am. here i am, you have no partner, here i am. all praise and blessings are yours, and all dominion. you have no partner. sahih al-bukhari 1549 · sahih muslim 1184 optional · if you fear you may not finish (illness, age) اللَّهُمَّ مَحِلِّي حَيْثُ حَبَسْتَنِي allāhumma maḥillī ḥaythu ḥabastanī meaning: o allah, i will leave ihram wherever you stop me. sahih al-bukhari 5089 · sahih muslim 1207 now in ihram: avoid perfume or scented soap, cream or wipes cutting or removing hair or nails marital relations and intimacy; a marriage contract hunting animals arguing, bad language, sins men: fitted, stitched clothing (shirts, trousers, underwear); covering the head women: niqab and gloves qur’an 2:197 · sahih al-bukhari 1542, 1838 allowed in ihram showering with unscented soap · changing your ihram sheets · watch, glasses, belt, money pouch · umbrella · bandages and medicine. remember flying in? most scholars say enter ihram before the plane passes the meeqat, not after landing at jeddah. some allow jeddah for certain routes. follow your scholar. made a mistake in ihram? don’t panic. things done by forgetting or not knowing are treated gently; some mistakes need a compensation (fidyah). ask a scholar. back next · step 3 enter makkah

title: Step 3 · Entering Makkah
text: step 3 of 8 entering makkah 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 step 03 entering makkah مكة you are in ihram now. keep saying the talbiyah, settle in, and get ready for the masjid. where am i? on the way to makkah / at your hotel what do i do now? 1 keep saying the talbiyah on the way. sunnah 2 check in and rest if you need to. it is fine to sleep or eat before tawaf. a rested pilgrim makes fewer mistakes. optional 3 take a bath if easy, then make wudu. the prophet ﷺ bathed before entering makkah. wudu is needed for tawaf. wudu: must for tawaf 4 agree a meeting point with your group. pick a masjid gate by its number and name. write it in my info . practical 5 take only what you need. water, phone, charger, a bag for your shoes, this guide. what do i say? talbiyah, until you begin tawaf لَبَّيْكَ اللَّهُمَّ لَبَّيْكَ، لَبَّيْكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ لَبَّيْكَ، إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ وَالنِّعْمَةَ لَكَ وَالْمُلْكَ، لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ labbayka-llāhumma labbayk. labbayka lā sharīka laka labbayk. inna-l-ḥamda wa-n-ni‘mata laka wa-l-mulk. lā sharīka lak. meaning: here i am, o allah, here i am. here i am, you have no partner, here i am. all praise and blessings are yours, and all dominion. you have no partner. sahih al-bukhari 1549 · sahih muslim 1184 arriving at your hotel (a new place) أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ a‘ūdhu bi-kalimāti-llāhi-t-tāmmāti min sharri mā khalaq. meaning: i seek refuge in the perfect words of allah from the evil of what he has created. sahih muslim 2708 you can also remember allah in your own words, in any language. remember patience is part of your umrah expect crowds, heat and long walks. be gentle with others and with yourself. avoid leaving the hotel without knowing how to get back. take a photo of the hotel name and street. bath before entering makkah: sahih al-bukhari 1573 back next · step 4 enter the masjid

title: Step 4 · Entering Masjid al-Haram
text: step 4 of 8 entering the masjid 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 step 04 entering masjid al-haram the great mosque around the ka‘bah. enter calmly and walk to the tawaf area (the mataf ). where am i? at a gate of masjid al-haram what do i do now? 1 note your gate. take a photo of the gate number and name. put your shoes in your bag. practical 2 step in with your right foot and say the entry dua. sunnah 3 walk to the mataf. very crowded? tawaf on the upper floors is valid too. it is longer, but calmer. your choice 4 when you see the ka‘bah, make dua. ask allah for anything, in your own language. there is no fixed dua you must say here. 5 if the prayer is starting, join it first. then begin tawaf. what do i say? entering (right foot first) بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ، اللَّهُمَّ افْتَحْ لِي أَبْوَابَ رَحْمَتِكَ bismillāh, wa-ṣ-ṣalātu wa-s-salāmu ‘alā rasūlillāh. allāhumma-ftaḥ lī abwāba raḥmatik. meaning: in the name of allah, and peace and blessings on the messenger of allah. o allah, open for me the doors of your mercy. sahih muslim 713 · sunan abi dawud 465 leaving the masjid, left foot first اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ allāhumma innī as’aluka min faḍlik. meaning: o allah, i ask you from your bounty. sahih muslim 713 remember if you get lost go to the nearest gate, read its number, and call your group. masjid staff can help. open my info avoid stopping in walkways for photos. letting children walk ahead without a meeting plan. women on their period wait before entering for tawaf. read what to do back next · step 5 begin tawaf

title: Step 5 · Tawaf
text: step 5 of 8 tawaf 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 step 05 · essential tawaf الطواف walk around the ka‘bah 7 times , with the ka‘bah on your left , starting and ending at the black stone. where am i? in the mataf, around the ka‘bah anticlockwise. ka‘bah always on your left . look for the green light on the masjid wall in line with the black stone. what do i do now? before you start have wudu. stop saying the talbiyah. men: uncover the right shoulder (sheet under the right arm, over the left shoulder), only for this tawaf. 1 stand in line with the black stone. intend tawaf in your heart. must 2 touch or kiss the black stone only if easy. usually it isn’t. just face it, raise your right hand toward it and say “allāhu akbar”. sunnah 3 walk with the ka‘bah on your left. go around the outside of the low curved wall (hijr isma‘il). it is part of the ka‘bah. must 4 men: walk briskly in rounds 1 to 3, if you can. short, quick steps (ramal). normal pace in rounds 4 to 7. skip it in heavy crowds. sunnah 5 at the yemeni corner, touch it with your right hand if easy. if not, just walk on. no need to point. sunnah 6 each time you pass the black stone line: one round done. raise your right hand and say “allāhu akbar”. tap the counter below. 7 after round 7, tawaf is complete. men: cover your right shoulder again. round counter you are on round 1 of 7 alhamdulillah 7 rounds done 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 i passed the black stone +1 undo lost count? go with the lower number you are sure of. what do i say? at the black stone, every round اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ allāhu akbar meaning: allah is the greatest. sahih al-bukhari 1613. many also say “bismillāh” first, reported from ibn ‘umar. between the yemeni corner and the black stone رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ rabbanā ātinā fi-d-dunyā ḥasanah, wa fi-l-ākhirati ḥasanah, wa qinā ‘adhāba-n-nār. meaning: our lord, give us good in this world and good in the hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the fire. qur’an 2:201 · sunan abi dawud 1892 suggested during tawaf: the dua of ibrahim and isma‘il رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّا إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ rabbanā taqabbal minnā, innaka anta-s-samī‘u-l-‘alīm. meaning: our lord, accept this from us. you are the all-hearing, the all-knowing. qur’an 2:127 · a suggestion, not required the rest of the time: your own words there is no fixed dua for each round. make dua in any language, remember allah, or recite qur’an. more suggested duas remember prayer called during tawaf? join the prayer where you are. then continue from that point. wudu broke during tawaf? leave, renew your wudu and come back. scholars differ on whether you continue or restart. ask your scholar. tired or in a wheelchair? tawaf in a wheelchair, or on the upper floors, is valid. see care guidance avoid these mistakes walking inside hijr isma‘il. that round does not count. pushing to reach the black stone. hurting others is a sin; touching it is only sunnah. touching the ka‘bah cloth in ihram. it is perfumed. loud group duas and stopping in the flow for photos. back next · step 6 after tawaf

title: Step 6 · After Tawaf
text: step 6 of 8 after tawaf 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 step 06 after tawaf pray two short rak‘ahs, drink zamzam, then head to safa for sa‘i. where am i? near maqam ibrahim, or anywhere in the masjid what do i do now? 1 men: cover both shoulders. 2 pray 2 rak‘ahs behind maqam ibrahim if there is space. if crowded, pray anywhere in the masjid. don’t pray in the path of people doing tawaf. recite surah al-kafirun and surah al-ikhlas, one in each rak‘ah (sahih muslim 1218). strongly recommended some scholars consider these 2 rak‘ahs required. 3 drink zamzam water and make dua. coolers of zamzam are all around the masjid. sunnah 4 if easy, touch the black stone once more. only if it is not crowded. otherwise skip it. sunnah, if easy 5 follow the signs to the mas‘a (safa and marwah). resting briefly first is fine. what do i say? walking to maqam ibrahim (optional) وَاتَّخِذُوا مِنْ مَقَامِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ مُصَلًّى wattakhidhū min maqāmi ibrāhīma muṣallā. meaning: and take the standing place of ibrahim as a place of prayer. qur’an 2:125 · recited by the prophet ﷺ here, sahih muslim 1218 drinking zamzam ask allah for whatever you need, in your own words. “zamzam water is for whatever it is drunk for.” sunan ibn majah 3062 remember praying at sunrise, noon or sunset? some scholars say wait until these times pass; others allow these 2 rak‘ahs at any time. follow your scholar. multazam (optional) some companions made dua at the wall between the black stone and the door. only if not crowded, and don’t touch the perfumed cloth in ihram. back next · step 7 begin sa‘i at safa

title: Step 7 · Sa‘i
text: step 7 of 8 sa‘i 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 step 07 · essential sa‘i السعي walk between the hills of safa and marwah 7 times. start at safa, finish at marwah. about 3 km in all. where am i? the mas‘a: the long hall of safa and marwah what do i do now? 1 go to safa. as you get near, recite the verse (first time only). sunnah 2 on safa, face the ka‘bah and raise your hands. say “allāhu akbar” three times and the dhikr below, then make your own dua. repeat three times. sunnah 3 walk to marwah. that is lap 1. must: 7 laps, safa first 4 men: jog lightly between the green lights. women walk normally the whole way. sunnah 5 on marwah, face the ka‘bah and do the same as on safa. (not the verse.) then walk back to safa: lap 2. 6 lap 7 ends at marwah. sa‘i is complete. lap tracker you are on lap 1 of 7 safa marwah alhamdulillah sa‘i complete you should be at marwah. 1 s→m 2 m→s 3 s→m 4 m→s 5 s→m 6 m→s 7 s→m i reached the hill +1 undo what do i say? approaching safa, first lap only إِنَّ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةَ مِنْ شَعَائِرِ اللَّهِ ۝ أَبْدَأُ بِمَا بَدَأَ اللَّهُ بِهِ inna-ṣ-ṣafā wa-l-marwata min sha‘ā’iri-llāh. abda’u bimā bada’a-llāhu bih. meaning: indeed safa and marwah are among the signs of allah. i begin with what allah began with. qur’an 2:158 · sahih muslim 1218 on safa and on marwah, facing the ka‘bah اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ. لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ، وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ، لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ، أَنْجَزَ وَعْدَهُ، وَنَصَرَ عَبْدَهُ، وَهَزَمَ الْأَحْزَابَ وَحْدَهُ allāhu akbar (×3). lā ilāha illa-llāhu waḥdahū lā sharīka lah, lahu-l-mulku wa lahu-l-ḥamd, wa huwa ‘alā kulli shay’in qadīr. lā ilāha illa-llāhu waḥdah, anjaza wa‘dah, wa naṣara ‘abdah, wa hazama-l-aḥzāba waḥdah. meaning: allah is the greatest. none has the right to be worshipped but allah alone, without partner. his is the dominion and the praise, and he has power over all things. none has the right to be worshipped but allah alone. he fulfilled his promise, helped his servant, and alone defeated the allied forces. sahih muslim 1218 · say it 3 times, with your own dua in between between the hills (reported from the companions) رَبِّ اغْفِرْ وَارْحَمْ، إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْأَعَزُّ الْأَكْرَمُ rabbi-ghfir warḥam, innaka anta-l-a‘azzu-l-akram. meaning: my lord, forgive and have mercy. you are the most mighty, the most generous. reported from companions, not from the prophet ﷺ · musannaf ibn abi shaybah; al-bayhaqi 5/95 while walking: your own words no fixed dua is required between the hills. make dua, dhikr or recite qur’an. ideas for dhikr remember you may rest and drink sit down between laps if you need to. wudu is recommended for sa‘i, but most scholars say it is not required. wheelchair? sa‘i in a wheelchair is valid. there are wheelchair lanes and upper floors. care guidance avoid these mistakes starting at marwah. that first lap doesn’t count. counting there-and-back as one lap. safa → marwah is one; marwah → safa is the next. running the whole way. the light jog is only for men, only between the green lights. back next · step 8 shave or cut hair

title: Step 8 · Halq or Taqsir
text: step 8 of 8 halq / taqsir 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 step 08 · essential · last step shave or shorten your hair this is the last act of umrah. it ends your ihram. halq = shave. taqsir = shorten. where am i? after sa‘i: barbers near the marwah exits, or your hotel what do i do now? men must a shave the whole head. this is better: the prophet ﷺ made dua three times for those who shave. best b or shorten hair from all over the head. not just a few strands from one side. scholars differ on the minimum women must 1 gather your hair together. in private: at your hotel, by yourself, a mahram, or another woman. 2 cut about a fingertip’s length from the ends. roughly 2 cm. women do not shave. what do i say? nothing specific is required. thank allah in your own words. a simple word of thanks الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ al-ḥamdu lillāh meaning: all praise is for allah. remember use a new, clean blade ask the barber to open a fresh blade in front of you. avoid changing out of ihram clothes, or using perfume, before your hair is cut. dua for those who shave: sahih al-bukhari 1727, sahih muslim 1301 · women shorten, not shave: sunan abi dawud 1984 back finish umrah complete

title: Umrah complete
text: all 8 steps done umrah complete الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ your umrah is complete. may allah accept it from you. what changes now? all ihram restrictions are lifted. you may wear normal clothes and use perfume. keep praying in the masjid and doing extra (voluntary) tawaf, which needs no ihram. a greeting pilgrims share تَقَبَّلَ اللَّهُ مِنَّا وَمِنْكُمْ taqabbala-llāhu minnā wa minkum meaning: may allah accept from us and from you. farewell tawaf when leaving makkah? required after hajj. for umrah, scholars differ. many recommend it. ask your scholar. what comes next? visiting madinah (optional, not part of umrah) going to madinah? book a free rawdah (riyad al-jannah) permit in the nusuk app before you go; you can only enter in your time slot. the haramain train takes about 2 hours from makkah to madinah. duas to keep making share this free guide with family after you return home arriving back (added to the travel dua) آيِبُونَ، تَائِبُونَ، عَابِدُونَ، لِرَبِّنَا حَامِدُونَ āyibūna, tā’ibūna, ‘ābidūna, li-rabbinā ḥāmidūn. meaning: we return, repenting, worshipping, and praising our lord. sahih muslim 1342 keep one good habit you built on the trip: a prayer on time, daily dhikr, or reading qur’an. tell the people on your dua list that you prayed for them. help someone else prepare: share this free guide. back to home

subḥāna-llāh glory be to allah الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ al-ḥamdu lillāh all praise is for allah لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ lā ilāha illa-llāh none is worthy of worship but allah اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ allāhu akbar subḥāna-llāhi-l-‘aẓīm glory and praise be to allah; glory be to allah the magnificent no might nor power: “a treasure of paradise”, sahih al-bukhari 4205 · subḥāna-llāhi wa bi-ḥamdih…: “light on the tongue, heavy in the balance”, sahih al-bukhari 6682 sending blessings on the prophet ﷺ (full) اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ، كَمَا صَلَّيْتَ عَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ، اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ، كَمَا بَارَكْتَ عَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ allāhumma ṣalli ‘alā muḥammadin wa ‘alā āli muḥammad, kamā ṣallayta ‘alā āli ibrāhīm, innaka ḥamīdun majīd. allāhumma bārik ‘alā muḥammadin wa ‘alā āli muḥammad, kamā bārakta ‘alā āli ibrāhīm, innaka ḥamīdun majīd. meaning: o allah, send prayers on muhammad and the family of muhammad, as you sent prayers on the family of ibrahim; you are praiseworthy, glorious. o allah, bless muhammad and the family of muhammad, as you blessed the family of ibrahim; you are praiseworthy, glorious. sahih al-bukhari 3370 7 travel: leaving, journey, return leaving your home بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللَّهِ، لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ bismillāh, tawakkaltu ‘ala-llāh, lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh. meaning: in the name of allah. i put my trust in allah. there is no might nor power except with allah. sunan abi dawud 5095 (sahih) setting off on the journey (full travel dua) اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ. سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ، وَإِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ. اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّا نَسْأَلُكَ فِي سَفَرِنَا هَذَا الْبِرَّ وَالتَّقْوَى، وَمِنَ الْعَمَلِ مَا تَرْضَى. اللَّهُمَّ هَوِّنْ عَلَيْنَا سَفَرَنَا هَذَا وَاطْوِ عَنَّا بُعْدَهُ. اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ الصَّاحِبُ فِي السَّفَرِ، وَالْخَلِيفَةُ فِي الْأَهْلِ. اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ وَعْثَاءِ السَّفَرِ، وَكَآبَةِ الْمَنْظَرِ، وَسُوءِ الْمُنْقَلَبِ فِي الْمَالِ وَالْأَهْلِ allāhu akbar (×3). subḥāna-lladhī sakhkhara lanā hādhā wa mā kunnā lahū muqrinīn, wa innā ilā rabbinā la-munqalibūn. allāhumma innā nas’aluka fī safarinā hādha-l-birra wa-t-taqwā, wa mina-l-‘amali mā tarḍā. allāhumma hawwin ‘alaynā safaranā hādhā wa-ṭwi ‘annā bu‘dah. allāhumma anta-ṣ-ṣāḥibu fi-s-safar, wa-l-khalīfatu fi-l-ahl. allāhumma innī a‘ūdhu bika min wa‘thā’i-s-safar, wa ka’ābati-l-manẓar, wa sū’i-l-munqalabi fi-l-māli wa-l-ahl. meaning: allah is the greatest (three times). glory be to the one who has placed this at our service; we could not have done it ourselves, and to our lord we will surely return. o allah, we ask you on this journey for goodness and piety, and for deeds that please you. o allah, make this journey easy for us and shorten its distance. o allah, you are the companion on the journey and the one who looks after the family. o allah, i seek refuge in you from the hardship of travel, from distressing sights, and from an evil return to wealth and family. sahih muslim 1342 arriving at a new place (hotel, rest stop) أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ a‘ūdhu bi-kalimāti-llāhi-t-tāmmāti min sharri mā khalaq. meaning: i seek refuge in the perfect words of allah from the evil of what he has created. sahih muslim 2708 returning home (add to the travel dua) آيِبُونَ، تَائِبُونَ، عَابِدُونَ، لِرَبِّنَا حَامِدُونَ āyibūna, tā’ibūna, ‘ābidūna, li-rabbinā ḥāmidūn. meaning: we return, repenting, worshipping, and praising our lord. sahih muslim 1342 8 suggested for tawaf & sa‘i suggestions, not requirements these are authentic duas from the qur’an and sunnah that suit tawaf and sa‘i. none of them is fixed to a round or lap. use any, in any order, or your own words. the dua of ibrahim and isma‘il, building the ka‘bah رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّا إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ rabbanā taqabbal minnā, innaka anta-s-samī‘u-l-‘alīm. meaning: our lord, accept this from us. you are the all-hearing, the all-knowing. qur’an 2:127 asking forgiveness (the dua of adam and his wife) رَبَّنَا ظَلَمْنَا أَنْفُسَنَا وَإِنْ لَمْ تَغْفِرْ لَنَا وَتَرْحَمْنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ rabbanā ẓalamnā anfusanā wa in lam taghfir lanā wa tarḥamnā la-nakūnanna mina-l-khāsirīn. meaning: our lord, we have wronged ourselves. if you do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we will surely be among the losers. qur’an 7:23 the best way to ask forgiveness (sayyid al-istighfar) اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ رَبِّي، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، خَلَقْتَنِي وَأَنَا عَبْدُكَ، وَأَنَا عَلَى عَهْدِكَ وَوَعْدِكَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ، أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا صَنَعْتُ، أَبُوءُ لَكَ بِنِعْمَتِكَ عَلَيَّ، وَأَبُوءُ لَكَ بِذَنْبِي، فَاغْفِرْ لِي، فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ allāhumma anta rabbī, lā ilāha illā ant, khalaqtanī wa ana ‘abduk, wa ana ‘alā ‘ahdika wa wa‘dika mastaṭa‘t, a‘ūdhu bika min sharri mā ṣana‘t, abū’u laka bi-ni‘matika ‘alayy, wa abū’u laka bi-dhanbī, faghfir lī, fa-innahū lā yaghfiru-dh-dhunūba illā ant. meaning: o allah, you are my lord; none has the right to be worshipped but you. you created me and i am your servant. i keep your covenant and promise as best i can. i seek refuge in you from the evil i have done. i acknowledge your favour on me, and i acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, for none forgives sins but you. sahih al-bukhari 6306 asking for pardon اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّكَ عَفُوٌّ تُحِبُّ الْعَفْوَ فَاعْفُ عَنِّي allāhumma innaka ‘afuwwun tuḥibbu-l-‘afwa fa‘fu ‘annī. meaning: o allah, you are the one who pardons, and you love to pardon, so pardon me. sunan ibn majah 3850 (sahih); also jami‘ at-tirmidhi 3513 for guidance and a firm heart رَبَّنَا لَا تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنَا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنَا وَهَبْ لَنَا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ رَحْمَةً إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْوَهَّابُ rabbanā lā tuzigh qulūbanā ba‘da idh hadaytanā wa hab lanā min ladunka raḥmah, innaka anta-l-wahhāb. meaning: our lord, do not let our hearts turn away after you have guided us, and grant us mercy from yourself. you are the giver. qur’an 3:8 o turner of hearts يَا مُقَلِّبَ الْقُلُوبِ ثَبِّتْ قَلْبِي عَلَى دِينِكَ yā muqalliba-l-qulūb, thabbit qalbī ‘alā dīnik. meaning: o turner of hearts, keep my heart firm on your religion. jami‘ at-tirmidhi 2140 (hasan) guidance, piety, chastity and contentment اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الْهُدَى وَالتُّقَى وَالْعَفَافَ وَالْغِنَى allāhumma innī as’aluka-l-hudā wa-t-tuqā wa-l-‘afāfa wa-l-ghinā. meaning: o allah, i ask you for guidance, piety, chastity, and freedom from need. sahih muslim 2721 for your parents رَبِّ ارْحَمْهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيَانِي صَغِيرًا rabbi-rḥamhumā kamā rabbayānī ṣaghīrā. meaning: my lord, have mercy on them both, as they raised me when i was small. qur’an 17:24 for your spouse and children رَبَّنَا هَبْ لَنَا مِنْ أَزْوَاجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّاتِنَا قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ وَاجْعَلْنَا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إِمَامًا rabbanā hab lanā min azwājinā wa dhurriyyātinā qurrata a‘yunin waj‘alnā li-l-muttaqīna imāmā. meaning: our lord, give us joy in our spouses and children, and make us leaders of the god-conscious. qur’an 25:74 the dua of ibrahim for prayer and family رَبِّ اجْعَلْنِي مُقِيمَ الصَّلَاةِ وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِي رَبَّنَا وَتَقَبَّلْ دُعَاءِ rabbi-j‘alnī muqīma-ṣ-ṣalāti wa min dhurriyyatī, rabbanā wa taqabbal du‘ā’. meaning: my lord, make me and my descendants steadfast in prayer. our lord, accept my dua. qur’an 14:40 praying for others when you pray for someone in their absence, an angel says: “and for you the same.” sahih muslim 2732 open my dua list

title: Women’s guidance
text: special guidance women e · women’s guidance umrah for women the steps are the same as for men, with a few differences. here they are, step by step. 2 ihram wear your normal loose, modest clothes, in any colour. there is no special ihram garment for women. do not wear a niqab (face veil) or gloves while in ihram. say the talbiyah quietly. covering the face near men many scholars allow lowering a cloth from the head over the face when non-mahram men are near. follow your scholar. no niqab or gloves: sahih al-bukhari 1838. the report of women lowering a cloth (sunan abi dawud 1833) is graded weak by al-albani; scholars rely on other reports. 5 tawaf & 7 sa‘i keep both shoulders covered. the right-shoulder uncovering is for men only. walk at a normal pace. no brisk walking in tawaf, no jogging between the green lights. you don’t need to reach the black stone. pointing is enough. in crowds, the outer edges and upper floors are calmer. 8 cutting hair gather your hair and cut about a fingertip’s length (≈2 cm) from the ends, in private. women do not shave. sunan abi dawud 1984 if your period starts don’t worry. your umrah is not lost. here is what to do. a before ihram? you can still enter ihram at the meeqat. take a bath for cleanliness, make the intention and say the talbiyah. b before tawaf? stay in ihram. do everything except tawaf. when your period ends, take a full bath (ghusl), then do tawaf, sa‘i and cut your hair. c after tawaf, before sa‘i? continue. you can do sa‘i and cut your hair. d your flight leaves before it ends? scholars give different answers. speak to a scholar before you travel if you can. “do everything a pilgrim does, except tawaf of the house, until you are clean.” sahih al-bukhari 305. ihram after childbirth bleeding: sahih muslim 1209. staying inside the masjid during a period most scholars say don’t stay in the masjid; some allow it. follow your scholar. medicine to delay a period many scholars permit it if it is safe for you. ask your doctor first. travelling travelling without a mahram saudi rules: since october 2022 the ministry of hajj and umrah no longer requires women to have a mahram for umrah. religious ruling: scholars differ. ask your scholar. back to step 5 · tawaf

title: Elderly, disabled and special circumstances
text: special guidance care & access e · special circumstances umrah is for everyone islam makes things easy. if walking, standing or crowds are hard for you, there is a way. elderly disabilities families first-timers good to know: these are all valid tawaf and sa‘i in a wheelchair or electric cart. the prophet ﷺ did tawaf riding, and told umm salamah, who was ill, to do tawaf riding. tawaf on the upper floors or roof. resting between tawaf and sa‘i, and sitting between laps of sa‘i. skipping sunnah acts you can’t do: brisk walking, jogging, touching the black stone. sahih al-bukhari 1607, 1619 elderly pilgrims 1 add the condition when entering ihram. “allāhumma maḥillī ḥaythu ḥabastanī.” if illness stops you, you can leave ihram without penalty. see step 2 2 rest first. go at quieter, cooler times. late night and early morning are usually calmer. 3 ask for a wheelchair or cart at the masjid. ask staff at the gates where to find them today; locations and options change. 4 carry water, medicines and a small snack. the condition, when entering ihram اللَّهُمَّ مَحِلِّي حَيْثُ حَبَسْتَنِي allāhumma maḥillī ḥaythu ḥabastanī meaning: o allah, i will leave ihram wherever you stop me. sahih al-bukhari 5089 · sahih muslim 1207 people with disabilities can’t walk? you may be pushed or carried for tawaf and sa‘i. low vision or blind? go with a companion. this guide works with screen readers, large text and audio. deaf or hard of hearing? every dua has written transliteration and meaning; agree hand signals with your group. can’t cut your own hair? anyone may cut it for you. continuous bleeding or incontinence many scholars say make wudu after the time for prayer begins and do tawaf with it. ask a scholar about your case. families & children a child’s umrah is valid , and the parent is rewarded. for a young child, the parent makes the intention and carries them. sahih muslim 1336 1 put an id band on every child. your phone number, hotel name and the child’s name. 2 photo each child every morning. so you can show what they are wearing today. 3 agree a meeting gate and teach it. “if you are lost, stay still and tell a guard: gate [number].” 4 take turns. one adult does tawaf while another rests with small children. check current rules for prams in the mataf. first-time pilgrims it is normal to feel overwhelmed. stop, breathe, open this guide. only 4 things are essential. everything else is a bonus. walk on the outer edge of the crowd. it is longer but calmer. use the round and lap counters so you don’t worry about counting. when unsure, ask your group leader or a scholar at the masjid. back to umrah steps

title: Common mistakes and questions
text: help mistakes & questions f · common mistakes easy to avoid, once you know ! can affect validity etiquette / sunnah ! can affect validity · step 2 passing the meeqat without entering ihram. enter ihram before. if it already happened, ask a scholar straight away (going back, or a compensation). ! can affect validity · step 5 walking through hijr isma‘il (the curved wall). walk outside it. a round through it doesn’t count; repeat that round. ! can affect validity · step 7 starting sa‘i at marwah, or counting there-and-back as one lap. start at safa. each one-way walk is one lap. finish at marwah. ! can affect validity · step 8 men cutting only a few hairs; leaving ihram before cutting. shave, or shorten from all over the head. cut first, then change clothes. sunnah · step 5 keeping the right shoulder bare all through ihram, even in prayer. bare it only during this tawaf. cover it for prayer. etiquette · step 5 pushing and hurting people to kiss the black stone. point with your right hand. kissing it is sunnah; harming others is not allowed. etiquette thinking a special dua must be read for each round, or reading loudly from a book in a group. speak to allah softly, in your own words. quick questions i lost count of my rounds. go with the lower number you are sure of, and continue. can i rest between tawaf and sa‘i? yes. do i need wudu for sa‘i? it is recommended. most scholars say it is not required. the prayer started during tawaf or sa‘i. join the prayer. then continue from where you stopped. i used scented soap by mistake. wash it off. if you forgot or didn’t know, most scholars say there is no penalty. can i shower in ihram? yes, with unscented soap. a few hairs falling out by accident is not a problem. must i touch or kiss the black stone? no. pointing toward it is enough. is tawaf on the upper floors valid? yes. can i do umrah on behalf of my parent? yes, for a parent who has passed away or is too old or ill to travel. the prophet ﷺ told a man to “perform hajj and umrah on behalf of your father”. do your own umrah first; then, for theirs, make the intention for them at the meeqat. sunan abi dawud 1810, 1811 (sahih). scholars differ on the details can i do more than one umrah on this trip? scholars differ. some allow it, going out to the meeqat (often masjid ‘a’ishah at tan‘im) for each one. others advise spending the time in extra tawaf and prayer instead. follow your scholar. can my child wear ihram? yes. a child’s umrah is valid and the parent is rewarded. for a young child, the parent makes the intention and helps them through each step. sahih muslim 1336. families & children can men wear a face mask in ihram? scholars differ. many allow it when there is a need, such as illness or dense crowds; others say men should not cover the face in ihram. follow your scholar. still unsure? ask your group leader or a scholar at the masjid. scholarly notes

title: Before you go · planner
text: step 1 · planner before you go countdown planner before you go a simple countdown so nothing is left to the last minute. tick as you go; your ticks are saved on this phone. 8 weeks eight weeks before choose your dates and how you will book: an approved umrah agent, or directly through nusuk. check your passport is valid for at least 6 months from your travel date. decide your visa: umrah visa, or a saudi visit or tourist visa. book the meningitis (acyw) vaccine now. it must be given at least 10 days before you arrive. elderly, pregnant, or living with a long-term condition? see your doctor about the trip, the heat and the walking. start walking every day. umrah means several kilometres on foot; sa‘i alone is about 3 km. 4 weeks four weeks before create your nusuk account (see the steps below). hotel booked in a licensed hotel and recorded in nusuk masar (needed for the umrah visa). airport transfers booked. going to madinah? book the haramain train through official saudi arabia railways channels. learn the 4 essential acts and practise the talbiyah out loud. women: read the women’s guidance. families: read care & access. 1 week one week before pack using the list in step 1. men: ihram in your hand luggage. medicines in original packs, with prescriptions, in your hand luggage. money: some saudi riyals in cash, and a bank card that works abroad. tell your bank you are travelling. phone: set up roaming, or plan to buy a saudi sim or esim on arrival (you will need your passport). install this guide on your phone and open every page once, so it works offline. fill in my info and print the quick card. start my dua list : ask family and friends what they would like you to pray for. 1 day the day you travel trim nails, remove unwanted hair, and take a bath (ghusl). plan where you will enter ihram. flying? you must be in ihram before the plane passes the meeqat, so many men put on the ihram at home or at the airport. passport, visa, nusuk permit and tickets in one pouch you keep on you. say the dua for leaving home and the travel dua (in duas & dhikr). nusuk, step by step 1 download nusuk only from the official app store. it is the official platform of the ministry of hajj and umrah. avoid look-alike apps and websites. 2 create your account. you will need your passport and visa details. 3 book your umrah permit. choose the date and time. you cannot enter for umrah before your permit time. 4 visiting madinah? book a rawdah permit. it is free. men and women have separate times. 5 keep your permits easy to show. take a screenshot in case you have no signal. health in the heat drink often , before you feel thirsty. zamzam is available all around the masjid. use an umbrella in the sun (allowed in ihram) and go at cooler times. feet: wear sandals you have walked in before. carry plasters for blisters. chafing (men in ihram): use an unscented anti-chafe cream or petroleum jelly. diabetes: carry snacks and your glucose kit; long walks can lower your sugar. signs of heat exhaustion dizziness, headache, nausea, heavy sweating or confusion. stop, get into shade, drink water, and ask for help. in an emergency in makkah, call 911. practical tips shoes: carry them in a small bag instead of leaving them at the door. it saves a long search afterwards. carry light: phone, water, this guide, a little cash, your hotel card. leave valuables at the hotel. crowds change with the season and prayer times. ask your group leader when it is usually calmer. charge up: a power bank keeps your guide, counters and nusuk permits working all day. avoid unofficial visa, nusuk or train websites that ask for payment. leaving the vaccine to the last week. it must be at least 10 days before arrival. brand-new shoes on the day of umrah. checked september 2026: vaccine rules, saudi ministry of health (umrah 1447h); permits and nusuk masar, ministry of hajj and umrah. rules change each season; check again before booking. step 1 next · step 2 enter ihram

title: Visiting Madinah
text: optional · after umrah visiting madinah optional · not part of umrah visiting madinah المدينة most pilgrims also visit the prophet’s mosque in madinah. it is a separate, blessed visit. your umrah is complete without it. where am i? madinah, at masjid an-nabawi why visit “one prayer in my mosque is better than a thousand prayers in any other mosque, except al-masjid al-haram.” sahih al-bukhari 1190 . it is one of only three mosques the prophet ﷺ encouraged travelling to. sahih al-bukhari 1189 what do i do? 1 enter the masjid with your right foot and say the entry dua. the same dua as in makkah. no ihram is needed in madinah. sunnah 2 pray two rak‘ahs to greet the masjid. as you would in any mosque, if it is not a prayer time. sunnah 3 pray in the rawdah, with your nusuk permit. “between my house and my pulpit is a garden of the gardens of paradise.” enter only in your booked time slot. men and women have separate times. permit needed 4 greet the prophet ﷺ, then abu bakr and ‘umar. walk calmly along the grave area, say salam softly, and keep moving with the line. 5 visit masjid quba. make wudu where you are staying, then go and pray there. the prophet ﷺ said this carries a reward like that of an umrah. sunnah 6 visit al-baqi‘ and the martyrs of uhud, if you wish. greet those buried there with the graveyard dua below, and pray for them. optional rawdah: sahih al-bukhari 1196 · quba: sunan ibn majah 1412 (hasan) what do i say? entering the masjid, right foot first بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ، اللَّهُمَّ افْتَحْ لِي أَبْوَابَ رَحْمَتِكَ bismillāh, wa-ṣ-ṣalātu wa-s-salāmu ‘alā rasūlillāh. allāhumma-ftaḥ lī abwāba raḥmatik. meaning: in the name of allah, and peace and blessings on the messenger of allah. o allah, open for me the doors of your mercy. sahih muslim 713 · sunan abi dawud 465 greeting at the grave of the prophet ﷺ السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ يَا أَبَا بَكْرٍ، السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ يَا عُمَرُ as-salāmu ‘alayka yā rasūla-llāh. as-salāmu ‘alayka yā abā bakr. as-salāmu ‘alayka yā ‘umar. meaning: peace be upon you, o messenger of allah. peace be upon you, o abu bakr. peace be upon you, o ‘umar. the greeting of ibn ‘umar, who said “o my father” for ‘umar · al-bayhaqi, al-sunan al-kubra 10271 visiting al-baqi‘ or any graveyard السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ أَهْلَ الدِّيَارِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُسْلِمِينَ، وَإِنَّا إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَلَاحِقُونَ، أَسْأَلُ اللَّهَ لَنَا وَلَكُمُ الْعَافِيَةَ as-salāmu ‘alaykum ahla-d-diyāri mina-l-mu’minīna wa-l-muslimīn, wa innā in shā’a-llāhu la-lāḥiqūn, as’alu-llāha lanā wa lakumu-l-‘āfiyah. meaning: peace be upon you, o believers and muslims who dwell here. we will, if allah wills, join you. i ask allah for well-being for us and for you. sahih muslim 975 leaving the masjid, left foot first اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ allāhumma innī as’aluka min faḍlik. meaning: o allah, i ask you from your bounty. sahih muslim 713 send blessings on the prophet ﷺ often the full salawat is in duas & dhikr. remember going from madinah to makkah for umrah? enter ihram at the madinah meeqat, dhul-hulayfah (abyar ‘ali), before you continue. the haramain train takes about 2 hours. rawdah permit book it in the nusuk app before you arrive. you cannot enter outside your slot. women visiting graveyards scholars differ on this. follow your scholar, and check the current visiting arrangements on site. avoid raising your voice in the masjid, especially near the grave. pushing in the rawdah or at the grave. give others space; everyone has limited time. stopping in the walkways and blocking the line. back keep going duas & dhikr

title: Glossary
text: reference glossary words you will hear glossary simple meanings for the words used in this guide, from a to z. black stone الحجر الأسود the stone set in one corner of the ka‘bah (al-hajar al-aswad). each round of tawaf starts and ends in line with it. step 5 dhikr ذِكْر remembering allah with short phrases, like subhanallah or alhamdulillah. dua دُعَاء a personal prayer or request to allah, in any language. fidyah فِدْيَة a compensation, such as feeding the poor or a sacrifice, for certain mistakes in ihram. ask a scholar. ghusl غُسْل a full bath that washes the whole body, for purification. halq حَلْق shaving the whole head (men). ends ihram. step 8 haram حَرَم the sacred area around makkah (and madinah). also used for masjid al-haram itself. hijr isma‘il (hatim) حِجْر إسماعيل the low, curved wall beside the ka‘bah. it is part of the ka‘bah, so tawaf goes around the outside of it. idtiba‘ اضْطِبَاع men uncovering the right shoulder during the tawaf of umrah only. ihram إحْرَام the sacred state of umrah, entered with intention and the talbiyah. also the two white sheets men wear. step 2 ka‘bah الكَعْبَة the cube-shaped house of allah in makkah, which muslims
